2 طنّخهُ , (K,) inf. n. تَطْنِيخٌ; (TA;) and ↓ اطنخهُ , (K,) inf. n. إِطْنَاخٌ; (TA;) It (grease [or greasy food], TA) caused him to suffer indigestion. (K, TA.) ―
-b2- Sh says, I heard ElFak'asee say, نَشْرَبُ هٰذِهِ الأَلْبَانَ فتطنخنا عَنِ الطَّعَامِ [i. e. فَتُطَنِّخُنَا or ↓ فَتُطْنِخُنَا ] meaning [We drink these milks and] they render us in no need, or serve us in stead, of [other] food. (L.) ―
-b3- And one says, طُنِّخَتِ النَّاقَةُ, and الدَّابَّة, meaning The she-camel, and the beast, became [or was rendered] very fat. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
